# Wrangler Source Maps Deploy and CI Integration

Date: 2026-08-23
Author: example.com
Status: production

## Symptom / Use-case

When a Workers script throws an unhandled exception in production, the stack trace points into the minified/bundled output — function names are mangled, line numbers reference the bundle rather than the original TypeScript source, and the error message alone is insufficient to locate the problem. Developers lose significant time manually correlating bundle positions back to source files.

Uploading source maps during the Wrangler deploy step enables Cloudflare to automatically symbolicate stack traces in the Workers dashboard and in Logpush exports. Engineers see original TypeScript file paths, line numbers, and function names in error reports — reducing mean time to diagnosis from hours to minutes.

## Context

Cloudflare Workers supports source map upload as part of the deploy flow. When `upload_source_maps = true` is set in `wrangler.toml`, Wrangler includes the generated `.map` files alongside the Worker bundle. Cloudflare stores these securely (they are never served to end users) and uses them to symbolicate stack traces in the `workers:exceptions` Logpush dataset and in the Workers dashboard error view.

Source maps must be generated by the build tool (esbuild, which Wrangler uses internally, or Vite/Rollup for custom builds). For TypeScript projects, esbuild must emit source maps that chain back to the original `.ts` files, not just to intermediate JavaScript.

## Enabling Source Maps in wrangler.toml

```toml
# wrangler.toml
name = "my-api"
main = "src/index.ts"
compatibility_date = "2026-01-01"

# Enable source map upload on every wrangler deploy
upload_source_maps = true
```

That is the complete configuration for projects that use Wrangler's built-in esbuild bundler. Wrangler automatically sets `--sourcemap` on the internal esbuild invocation when `upload_source_maps = true`.

## Custom Build Configuration (Vite / Rollup)

For projects that use a custom build step before `wrangler deploy`, configure the build tool to emit external source maps.

```typescript
// vite.config.ts (for a Worker built with Vite)
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    target: "es2022",
    ssr: true,            // prevents Vite from injecting browser polyfills
    outDir: "dist",
    rollupOptions: {
      input: "src/index.ts",
      output: {
        entryFileNames: "index.js",
        format: "es",
        // External source maps — Wrangler reads the .map file from dist/
        sourcemap: true,
      },
    },
    // Do not inline source maps — Wrangler uploads them separately
    minify: "esbuild",
  },
  resolve: {
    conditions: ["workerd", "worker", "browser"],
  },
});
```

```toml
# wrangler.toml (custom build)
name = "my-api"
main = "dist/index.js"   # pre-built output
compatibility_date = "2026-01-01"
upload_source_maps = true

[build]
command = "vite build"
```

Wrangler will automatically detect `dist/index.js.map` and upload it alongside `dist/index.js`.

## CI Pipeline Integration

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy-with-sourcemaps.yml
name: Deploy with Source Maps

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build (if using custom build)
        run: npm run build
        # For Wrangler's built-in bundler, skip this step

      - name: Verify source map exists
        run: |
          # Confirm the .map file was generated before deploying
          if [ ! -f "dist/index.js.map" ]; then
            echo "::error::Source map dist/index.js.map not found — aborting deploy"
            exit 1
          fi
          MAP_SIZE=$(wc -c < dist/index.js.map)
          echo "Source map size: ${MAP_SIZE} bytes"
          if [ "$MAP_SIZE" -lt 100 ]; then
            echo "::error::Source map is suspiciously small (${MAP_SIZE} bytes) — build may have failed silently"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Deploy Worker with source maps
        run: npx wrangler deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}

      - name: Verify source map upload
        run: node scripts/verify-sourcemap-upload.mjs
        env:
          CF_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }}
          CF_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          WORKER_NAME: my-api
```

## Source Map Upload Verification Script

```javascript
// scripts/verify-sourcemap-upload.mjs
// Polls the Workers API to confirm source maps are attached to the latest script version

const ACCOUNT_ID = process.env.CF_ACCOUNT_ID;
const TOKEN = process.env.CF_API_TOKEN;
const WORKER_NAME = process.env.WORKER_NAME;

const API = `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${ACCOUNT_ID}/workers`;

async function getLatestVersion() {
  const resp = await fetch(`${API}/scripts/${WORKER_NAME}/versions?limit=1`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` },
  });
  const data = await resp.json();
  if (!data.success) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(data.errors));
  return data.result[0];
}

async function checkSourceMapAttached(versionId) {
  const resp = await fetch(
    `${API}/scripts/${WORKER_NAME}/versions/${versionId}`,
    { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } }
  );
  const data = await resp.json();
  if (!data.success) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(data.errors));

  // The version metadata includes source_map_id when a map was uploaded
  return !!data.result?.metadata?.source_map_id;
}

const version = await getLatestVersion();
if (!version) {
  console.error("No versions found for Worker:", WORKER_NAME);
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log(`Latest version: ${version.id} (${version.metadata?.tag ?? "untagged"})`);

const hasMap = await checkSourceMapAttached(version.id);
if (!hasMap) {
  console.error(
    "::error::Source map was NOT uploaded with the latest version. " +
    "Check that upload_source_maps = true in wrangler.toml and the .map file was generated."
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log("Source map confirmed uploaded with latest Worker version.");
```

## Symbolication in Logpush

Configure a Logpush job for `workers:exceptions` to receive pre-symbolicated stack traces.

```bash
# Create a Logpush job for Workers exceptions (symbolicated)
curl -s -X POST \
  "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${CF_ACCOUNT_ID}/logpush/jobs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CF_API_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "workers-exceptions-symbolicated",
    "logpull_options": "fields=Exceptions,Outcome,ScriptName,ScriptVersion&timestamps=rfc3339",
    "destination_conf": "r2://my-logs-bucket/workers-exceptions?account-id='${CF_ACCOUNT_ID}'&access-key-id='${R2_ACCESS_KEY}'&secret-access-key='${R2_SECRET_KEY}'",
    "dataset": "workers_exceptions",
    "enabled": true,
    "output_options": {
      "field_delimiter": "\n",
      "record_template": "{\"timestamp\":\"{ClientRequestTime}\",\"outcome\":\"{Outcome}\",\"exceptions\":{Exceptions}}",
      "record_suffix": "\n",
      "timestamp_format": "rfc3339"
    }
  }'
```

A symbolicated exception entry in Logpush looks like:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-08-23T14:32:11Z",
  "outcome": "exception",
  "exceptions": [
    {
      "message": "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'email')",
      "stack": "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'email')\n    at getUserEmail (src/handlers/user.ts:42:18)\n    at handleRequest (src/index.ts:17:24)"
    }
  ]
}
```

Without source maps, `src/handlers/user.ts:42:18` would appear as `worker.js:1:38291`.

## Anti-patterns

- Inlining source maps in the Worker bundle (`sourcemap: 'inline'` in esbuild) — this dramatically increases bundle size and may push the script past the 10 MB uncompressed limit; always use external source maps
- Committing source maps to the git repository — they contain all original source code and should be treated as confidential artifacts; they are uploaded directly to Cloudflare, not stored in version control
- Setting `upload_source_maps = false` in the production environment while keeping it true in staging — production errors are the ones that need symbolication most
- Using source maps from a previous build (stale .map files) without rebuilding before deploy — the map will not match the deployed bundle and symbolication will produce garbage output
- Relying solely on Sentry or Datadog source map upload without also uploading to Cloudflare — Cloudflare symbolication works in the dashboard without any third-party integration

## Gotchas

- Source maps are tied to a specific Worker version; after a rollback to a previous version, errors will be symbolicated using the source map uploaded with that older version
- Wrangler does not upload source maps when using `wrangler dev` — symbolication only applies to deployed (production/staging) Workers
- The `sourceMappingURL` comment at the bottom of the bundle must reference a `.map` file that Wrangler can find; if the build tool writes an absolute path (e.g. `# sourceMappingURL=/path/to/project), Wrangler will fail to locate it — configure the build tool to use relative source map URLs
- Source maps uploaded to Cloudflare are stored encrypted and are never accessible via the CDN or public API — there is no risk of accidental exposure to end users
- `upload_source_maps = true` increases deploy time slightly because Wrangler must upload an additional file; on very large bundles with deep source trees, the map can be 2-5x the size of the bundle

## Verification

1. After deploy, navigate to the Workers dashboard → your Worker → Exceptions. Trigger a test error and confirm stack traces show TypeScript file paths and line numbers.
2. Run `wrangler tail` and trigger an error; confirm the `exception` event in the tail output includes a stack trace.
3. Use the verification script (`verify-sourcemap-upload.mjs`) in CI to assert `source_map_id` is present in the version metadata.
4. Compare a symbolicated stack frame line number against the TypeScript source: open `src/index.ts` at the reported line and confirm the code matches the error context.
